transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
Thousands of flights across the country are still delayed or cancelled following the FAA's
nationwide ground stop yesterday.
Christopher Allum from member station KQED reports from San Francisco International Airport.
A long line snakes around empty carousels at baggage claim.
There's been almost 300 cancelled flights here just today and nearly as many delays.
Travelers were eager to share their frustrations.
This is the United States of America.
This shouldn't not be happening to these people.
We have teachers that need to get back to their students.
Everyone's bags were everywhere.
No one was checking.
Anyone could walk up to anyone's bag and there were like hundreds of bags downstairs.
Just exhausted, tired, a bit frustrated of course as well.
But the main thing is we get home all right.
That was Sylvia Garcia, Lindsay Smith and Tim Fishel.
For NPR News, I'm Christopher Allum in San Francisco.
Much celebration in Texas as SpaceX's Starship made a triumphant return to Earth.
NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports the Starship landed on the same pad it took off from just
a day earlier.
Starship reentered Earth's atmosphere and swooped over the Baja Peninsula across Texas
to the same pad it took off from on the Gulf Coast.
Starship burst through low clouds and then lowered itself onto the pad where it was grabbed
by giant mechanical arms.
I still can't believe what we just saw.
That was insane.
That was wild.
Picture perfect.
The landing is a major breakthrough for SpaceX which seeks to one day make Starship a rapidly
reusable rocket.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
Ukrainian President Zelodmyr Zelensky says Washington proposed the idea of Ukraine ceding
land to Russia in exchange for NATO membership.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley has the story.
In comments reported by the AFP news agency, Zelensky said the U.S. had asked whether Ukraine
would withdraw from the eastern Donbass region if it is able to join NATO.
Zelensky said Ukraine is discussing specific security guarantees from NATO and the European
Union and that he would ask Ukrainians if they accepted the terms if formally offered.
Meanwhile, Putin is maintaining his position that Ukraine hand over territory Russia does
not control and he's rejected any foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine.
The Kremlin also renewed an old demand that NATO pull back military infrastructure from
central and eastern European countries that joined NATO following the breakup of the Soviet Union.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
A federal judge has ordered a two week delay to any work at an historic Washington public
golf course not far from the White House.
The order temporarily blocks President Donald Trump's push to redevelop the site.
You're listening to NPR.
NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is about to achieve a major long distance milestone.
NPR's John Stoness has more.
It's already flown farther from Earth than any man-made spacecraft ever.
But at just after 5 a.m. Eastern time on Wednesday, Voyager 1 will have traveled one light day
away from Earth.
That's about 16 billion miles or the distance light travels in 24 hours.
Voyager 1 launched with its twin Voyager 2 in 1977 and traveling at almost 38,000 miles
an hour discovered new moons and rings around both Jupiter and Saturn.
Voyager 2 took a different route to deep space in order to visit Uranus in Neptune.
It is scheduled to reach the light day milestone nine years from now.
John Stoness, NPR News.
A summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations begins on Tuesday in the Philippines.
One major focus for the Southeast Asian leaders, the U.S. and the Chinese representatives attending,
will be online scams that have swindled people and companies out of billions of dollars around
the globe.
The leaders have already expressed concerns about transnational criminal organizations
using scams and engaging in human trafficking.
Authorities have reported instances where workers have been lured into scam centers and
then subjected to threats against them.
Leaders attend in the event are planning to encourage information sharing among the nations
and strengthening international cooperation to dismantle the illegal operations.
I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.

SpaceX Starship lands back on its Texas launch pad, grabbed by mechanical arms after reentry
Zelensky says US asked if Ukraine would cede Donbas for NATO membership
Federal judge orders two-week delay on redevelopment of historic Washington public golf course near White House
NASA's Voyager 1 reaches one light day from Earth, about 16 billion miles away
ASEAN summit in the Philippines opens Tuesday, focusing on online scam centers and human trafficking
